title: Canonical data for the K-flat ordinary etale support comparison
statement: For ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and a closed-open pair $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$, $j:U\hookrightarrow P$, define the data of the coefficient support comparison as follows. Use the actual support sequence $S_A(I)=i_*H_A(I)\to I\to j_*j^*I$ of [lem-pur-etale-injective-support-sequence]. Using the existing total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], for a complex $Q$ its total-tensor row is $Q\otimes S_A(I)$, with its induced maps on morphisms of rows. For an $A$-linear chain map $a:Q\otimes I\to J$, a map $v:Q\otimes j_*j^*I\to j_*j^*J$ is the specified quotient map when, on every summand $Q^p\otimes(j_*j^*I)^q$ in total degree $n=p+q$, it is the ordinary adjoint of the pullback tensor comparison followed by $1\otimes\varepsilon_{j^*I^q}$, the inverse pullback tensor comparison, and $j^*(\iota_{p,q}a^n)$. Thus all summands, with their total-complex signs, are fixed. For a K-flat augmentation $Q\to B_P$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a representing isomorphism $Q_{!D}I\simeq L$, define $Q_{!D}(Q\otimes I)\simeq\operatorname{Res}(T_PL)$ by localized signed symmetry, the one-sided K-flat comparison, the augmentation and representing isomorphism, followed by the normalized scalar/tensor isomorphism of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Across a replacement $a$ its target identification is $(Q_{!D}a)^{-1}$ followed by this identification. The quotient identifications are the support-sequence computations of $Rj_*j^*$ followed by the same representing isomorphisms. Define the coefficient projection $T_PRj_{*,A}j^*L\to Rj_{*,B}j^*T_PL$ as the normalized scalar mate [lem-pur-etale-scalar-mate-projection] followed by inverse scalar/pullback comparison. Its restricted version is restriction of this map followed by the canonical direct-image and inverse-image scalar-restriction comparisons of [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. No strict $B$-action on $Q$, $I$ or $J$ is included.
